_metadata.description: National visa issuance and petition trends by fiscal year

sources.f1_issuances: U.S. State Department, Table XV(B)/XVI(B) - Nonimmigrant Visas Issued by Classification. FY2005-2009 from FY2009 Annual Report; FY2010-2014 from FY2014 Annual Report; FY2015-2019 from FY2019 Annual Report; FY2020-2024 from FY2024 Annual Report. Wikipedia F visa article used to cross-check.
sources.j1_issuances: U.S. State Department, Table XV(B)/XVI(B) - same source as F-1
sources.j1_participants: BridgeUSA Facts and Figures Excel (j1_participation_cy2015_2025.xlsx) - calendar year program begin dates, all categories combined
sources.h1b_issuances: U.S. State Department, Table XV(B)/XVI(B) - visa stamps issued at consulates
sources.h1b_petitions_approved: USCIS H-1B trend tables (FY2007-2017) and H-1B Petitions Annual Report to Congress (FY2019-2024). Note: petitions approved != visas issued; petitions include extensions, amendments, changes of employer. FY2018 unavailable (gap between trend tables and annual reports).
sources.o1_issuances: U.S. State Department, Table XV(B)/XVI(B) - visa stamps issued at consulates
sources.o1a_petitions_approved: USCIS STEM-Related Petition Trends factsheet (FY2018-2023). Note: O-1A only (sciences/education/business/athletics), excludes O-1B (arts)
sources.l1_issuances: U.S. State Department, Table XV(B)/XVI(B) - visa stamps issued at consulates. FY2007-2022 from Wikipedia L-1 visa article (sourced from State Dept annual reports); FY2023-2024 from VisaGrader.com (sourced from State Dept). Cross-checked FY2013-2022 between both sources.

notes: All fiscal year data follows the U.S. government fiscal year (Oct 1 - Sep 30). E.g., FY2024 = Oct 2023 - Sep 2024.
State Dept issuance counts = visa stamps issued at consulates abroad. Does NOT include status changes within the US.
USCIS petition counts = I-129 petitions approved domestically. Includes new employment, extensions, amendments, changes of employer.
The two measures (issuances vs petitions) are complementary but NOT additive - they measure different things.
J-1 participant data from BridgeUSA uses calendar year program begin dates, NOT fiscal year. CY2025 is partial (through ~March).
FY2020-2021 numbers across all categories significantly depressed due to COVID-19 pandemic and consular closures.

f1_issuances._unit: visa stamps issued at U.S. consulates abroad

j1_issuances._unit: visa stamps issued at U.S. consulates abroad

j1_participants_by_category._unit: BridgeUSA participants by calendar year program begin date

2025._note: Partial year - data through approximately March 2025

h1b_issuances._unit: visa stamps issued at U.S. consulates abroad

h1b_petitions_approved._unit: USCIS I-129 petitions approved (includes new, extensions, amendments, changes of employer)
h1b_petitions_approved._note: FY2007-2017 from USCIS trend tables (approvals for petitions received in that FY, actual approval may be later). FY2019-2024 from Annual Reports to Congress (all approvals during that FY regardless of when filed). FY2018 data not available from either source.

o1_issuances._unit: O-1 visa stamps issued at U.S. consulates abroad (O-1A + O-1B combined)

o1a_petitions_approved._unit: USCIS I-129 O-1A petitions approved (sciences/education/business/athletics only, excludes O-1B arts)
o1a_petitions_approved._source: USCIS STEM-Related Petition Trends: EB-2 and O-1A Categories factsheet

l1_issuances._unit: visa stamps issued at U.S. consulates abroad (L-1A + L-1B combined, includes blanket L petitions processed at consulates)
